judgements.justification: In A, Reviewer_Q5eH wrongly said the paper studies infinite-width networks and Reviewer_ab3Y wrongly called it a random-features analysis; both criticisms fed their 6s, the rebuttal corrected Q5eH, and no B reviewer made these errors.

added.name: Area chair set the award above reviewers' scores
added.definition: One committee's area chair recommended a higher tier than its reviewers' ratings and arguments supported, on the chair's own reading, often with a meta-review that overstates reviewer consensus.
added.justification: R01 concerns a reviewer's factual error; no existing reason covers a chair lifting the outcome above the reviews, which here is why A matched B's spotlight despite lower scores.

added.name: Enthusiastic low-confidence review carried weight
added.definition: One committee had a reviewer whose high score rested on enthusiasm rather than specifics, often at low confidence, and that score or wording raised the committee's ratings or shaped its meta-review.
added.justification: No existing reason covers a thin champion review inflating one committee's scores and meta-review; PKyu's 8 is part of why B's mean (7.0) exceeds A's (6.25).

added.name: Authors disclosed a flaw to one committee only
added.definition: The authors revealed an error or weakness in the paper on one committee's forum and not on the other's, so the two committees judged different information.
added.justification: No existing reason covers an information asymmetry created by the authors; this is a divergence in what the committees knew.

added.name: Committee discounted a known substantive flaw
added.definition: One committee learned of a substantive flaw, raised by a reviewer or admitted by the authors, yet its scores and meta-review did not weigh it, accepting a fix on trust or ignoring it.
added.justification: R04 covers who was told; this covers how a committee that knew of a flaw weighed it, a separate mechanism no existing reason names.

added.name: Rebuttal moved scores in one committee only
added.definition: The authors' rebuttal led one committee's reviewers to raise or lower their scores while the other committee's scores did not move, widening or narrowing the gap between them.
added.justification: No existing reason covers a rebuttal acting differently on the two committees; sDSa's raise is one source of B's higher mean.

reasoning: Both committees recommended a spotlight, so I judged divergences short of the recommendation. Scores diverged (A 6, 6, 6, 7; B 7, 6, 8, 8, 6), and the committees reached the same tier by different routes. R01 applies because two A reviewers misread the setting and criticized on that basis. A's spotlight came from the chair's own reading over borderline scores (R02). B's higher scores drew on a praise-only, low-confidence 8 that the meta-review copied (R03) and on one rebuttal-driven raise (R06). The authors disclosed the Theorem 1.1 error only to B (R04), and B accepted the fix on trust without weighing it (R05). I added no reason for the shared weaknesses both committees treated as minor, since shared features explain agreement, not a difference.
